June 1820. No evidence exists to give a date of composition for the preface (see headnote).
 I rode one evening] For S’s account of the visit to Venice that suggested the poem, see L ii 36: ‘So
he [Byron] took me in his gondola — much against my will for I wanted to return to Clare at Mrs.
Hoppners who was anxiously waiting for me — across the laguna to a long sandy island which defends
Venise [sic] from the Adriatic. When we disembarked, we found his horses waiting for us, & we rode
along the sands of the sea talking.’
 the bank of land] The ‘Lido di Malamocco’ that acts as a coastal defence for Venice. Clara was buried
on the Lido on 25 September 1818. Cp. Marino Faliero IV i 13–15: ‘the Adrian wave/Rose o’er the city’s
murmur in the night,/Dashing against the outward Lido’s bulwark’.
 Adria] The Adriatic Sea.
